name: Food Product Development

objectives.text: Describe the basic steps food developers follow to turn an idea into a new food product
Identify the job common ingredients such as flour, sugar, fat, and eggs do in a simple recipe
Compare two versions of a food product to identify differences in ingredients, appearance, texture, and taste
Describe the appearance, aroma, texture, and flavor of a food sample using sensory vocabulary
Explain how a value-added product such as jam, cheese, or jerky increases the worth of a raw agricultural commodity
Conduct a simple taste test or consumer preference survey and summarize the results to guide a new food product idea
Modify a basic recipe by changing one ingredient and record how the change affects the finished product
Summarize the factors that shape the planning of a new food product, including creativity, cost, nutrition, and regulation
Classify current consumer market demands such as local, organic, non-GMO, plant-based, and convenience foods that drive new product ideas
Conduct a sensory evaluation using a hedonic scale or triangle test and interpret the panel results
Explain how reactions such as Maillard browning, fermentation, emulsification, and gelatinization determine the quality of a formulated food product
Analyze the nutritional composition of a formulation and adjust ingredients to meet a target such as reduced sodium or added protein
Develop a standardized formula with ingredient weights and baker's or formula percentages that scales from a bench-top batch to a larger run
Identify how pH, water activity, and preservatives in a formulation affect the safety and shelf stability of a new food product
Plan a supervised agricultural experience project that develops and test-markets a value-added food product from a farm or home commodity
Explain the regulatory requirements a new food product must meet, including the ingredient statement, allergen declaration, Nutrition Facts panel, and permitted claims
Calculate ingredient cost per unit and a suggested price to judge the economic feasibility of a product concept
Analyze how food companies apply innovations such as alternative proteins, functional ingredients, or novel processing methods to create new products
Evaluate a prototype food product against sensory, nutritional, market, and regulatory targets and recommend reformulation
Design a new food product from concept through prototype, including formulation, sensory testing, nutrition labeling, and costing, that meets a specific consumer trend
Defend product development decisions with test data when presenting a food product concept to a judging panel such as the FFA Food Science and Technology CDE

changes: Kept all six original competencies, rewording some for precision (sensory comparison, consumer testing, prototype evaluation, capstone design). Replaced the vague grade 9 prototype objective with distinct skills in planning factors, market demand types, and formal sensory evaluation. Added missing competencies: ingredient functions, value-added concepts, recipe modification, food chemistry, nutritional reformulation, standardized formulas and scale-up, shelf stability, regulatory labeling, costing, industry innovation, an SAE product project, and an FFA CDE style defense. Left supply chains, packaging, distribution, and careers to sibling sub-topics.
